$comment: THE SINGLE DEFINITION OF SKILL_INVOCATION_PROVENANCE v1. There is no other.
This block used to be described in three places at once: a regex in
validate-provenance-block.sh (the READER), an example in gate-validation.md Check 17
(the SPEC), and an example in team-roles/adversary.md (the INSTRUCTION the agent reads).
Three hand-synchronised copies of one schema, in three languages, with nothing comparing
them. They diverged: adversary.md taught a bare ``` fence with no terminator, the
adversary emitted exactly what it was shown, the reader's regex matched nothing, and
validate-provenance-block.sh reported 'no provenance block required or present' and exited
0. Two full adversarial passes of the reference consumer's sprint 290 went unadjudicated
and the gate called them clean. An unparseable block scores exactly like a clean artifact.
So: the reader LOADS this file. The example every agent is taught is RENDERED from this
file. scripts/sync-taught-schema.sh --check fails the build if any rendered example has
drifted, or if any provenance example exists in an agent-read file that was NOT rendered
from here. Add a field here and it appears in the parser and in every doc at once.
Do not hand-write a provenance example anywhere. Render it.

envelope.$comment: The delimiters are load-bearing. A ``` code fence is not a provenance block: nothing parses it.

fields.name: skill
fields.doc: the evaluation that ACTUALLY RAN. Naming one you did not invoke is a forged block.

fields.name: invoked_at
fields.doc: Check 24 orders the pass series on this. Ambiguity here reorders the cycle.

fields.name: tool_use_id
fields.placeholder: <toolu_... — from the Skill tool response, or the Agent dispatch that spawned you>
fields.doc: the id of the Skill/Agent call that ran this evaluation. CHECKED FOR SHAPE ONLY — nothing verifies it against a transcript, so it is not proof the evaluation ran.

fields.name: mode
fields.forbidden_reason: Rule 20 requires mode: subagent. Dispatch the evaluation to a real subagent; single-voice sub-skills go to a Rule-19-bound teammate; the convergence review goes to the `adversary` role. Solo defeats independent evaluation.

fields.name: lead_role
fields.placeholder: <the step file that invoked or dispatched the evaluation>

fields.name: transcript_path
fields.doc: required for retro party-mode; byte-matched by validate-retro-evidence.sh.

fields.name: artifact
fields.enforced_by: Check 24 arm A (validate-adversarial-convergence.sh), not Check 17. Named here so the taught example carries it; asserted there, where the series is in scope.

fields.name: artifact_sha
fields.placeholder: <sha256 of that file, as you read it>
fields.doc: `shasum -a 256 <artifact> | cut -d' ' -f1`. Makes the pass a notarization of the bytes it reviewed, which is what lets the gate later prove a claimed revert landed on a state some pass actually saw.
fields.enforced_by: Check 24 arm A (validate-adversarial-convergence.sh), not Check 17. Named here so the taught example carries it; asserted there, where the series is in scope.

fields.name: findings_critical
fields.doc: the residue the verdict is adjudicated against. Required of EVERY known evaluation, not only verdict-bearing ones — see rules.counts_always.

fields.name: findings_critical_prior_scope
fields.doc: of the CRITICALs above, those in text the PRIOR pass also reviewed. OPTIONAL BY DESIGN: absent means the validator assumes ALL of them (fail-closed). Requiring it would invert that default and reject the safe omission. This is what separates 'not converging' from 'the document is moving'.

fields.name: findings_major
fields.doc: omit it and the stall rung goes silent for the ENTIRE series.

fields.name: findings_minor
fields.doc: the nitpick bucket. Does not block the exit condition.

fields.name: resolves_divergence
fields.doc: ONLY on the verification pass, and only if the pass before you STOPPED.

fields.name: verdict
fields.doc: required on every adversarial-review pass. There is no free-text verdict.

$comment: A profile is a VIEW of the one field list — never a second copy of it. Docs differ in
which fields they show and which values are pinned; they must not differ in the envelope,
the field names, or the semantics. sync-taught-schema.sh renders every taught example
from a profile, so adding a field here reaches every doc that shows it, at once.
The findings_* fields are in this profile because rules.counts_always requires them of
every known evaluation. A profile that showed fewer fields than the reader demands is
precisely the drift this schema exists to prevent: the agent emits what it was taught,
the reader rejects it, and the gate fails on a block the doc told the agent to write.
No verdict — party-mode is measured, not gated. See rules.counts_always.scope.
retro-party-mode.title: a retro party-mode invocation

$comment: The terminal-pass residue transcribed onto EACH story file, required by Check 17's
story-readiness gate. It is NOT hand-authored: scripts/stamp-story-provenance.sh derives
every field from the terminal adversarial pass (the single source of truth) and computes
artifact_sha over the story BODY with provenance blocks stripped; scripts/validate-story-
provenance.sh re-derives the same and fails closed on any drift. The batch-invariant fields
(skill/invoked_at/tool_use_id/mode/lead_role/findings_*/verdict) are COPIED from the
terminal pass verbatim; artifact and artifact_sha are the ONLY per-story fields. Both are
`require`d here (not merely for-verdict) so the s291/s292 drift — one block with artifact_sha,
one without — is impossible by construction: the writer always emits them and the cross-check
always demands them. This profile-scoped requirement does not touch the global field flags,
so party-mode blocks (which carry no artifact_sha) are unaffected.
story-provenance.title: a terminal-pass residue stamped onto a story file

rules.$comment: Cross-field invariants the reader enforces. Named so a failure can cite the rule.

verdict_requires_counts.assert: when `verdict` is present, findings_critical / findings_major / findings_minor are present and non-empty
verdict_requires_counts.why: A verdict is adjudicated AGAINST a residue. A pass with a verdict and no counts turns the stall rung off for the whole series.
verdict_requires_counts.scope: Check 17 asserts the COUNTS a verdict is adjudicated against. It does NOT assert artifact/artifact_sha — those are Check 24 arm A's, and duplicating them here made Check 17 reject blocks arm A accepts.

counts_always.assert: findings_critical / findings_major / findings_minor are present and non-empty on EVERY known evaluation, verdict-bearing or not
counts_always.why: An evaluation that records no residue cannot be scored, and 30+ sprints of the reference consumer prove what that costs: of 831 bmad-party-mode / bmad-advanced-elicitation / bmad-review-adversarial-general / bmad-validate-prd blocks on disk, 16 carried any severity residue (0.7% for party-mode). ai-dlc-adversary-review carried it on 55 of 55, which is the ONLY reason anyone can say whether a convergence pass earns its cost — and the answer turned out to be interesting (pass 1 finds real defects; 12 of 13 second passes find no CRITICAL or MAJOR). The same question about party-mode and elicitation is unanswerable, not answered-negative. This rule makes it answerable. Counting is not adjudicating: the counts are recorded, and nothing here gates on them.
counts_always.scope: Counts ONLY. `verdict` stays optional by design — a verdict is a convergence-cycle exit signal that Check 24 orders into a series, and stamping one on a party-mode or elicitation pass would enrol it in a cycle it is not part of. These evaluations are MEASURED, not GATED.

no_solo.why: Rule 20. This assertion was once gated on `skill in known_skills`, which was vacuous and coupled the only teeth Check 17 has to the enum's membership — drop the skill field and the solo rejection silently stopped firing. It is unconditional now.

required_non_empty.assert: a required field present with an empty value is a failure
required_non_empty.why: The parser accepts `key:` with the value on indented lines below, so presence and answeredness are different questions. A blank required field must not read like a supplied one.

parser.$comment: How the reader tokenises the block body. Stated here so the docs and the reader cannot disagree about it either.
parser.continuation: an INDENTED line continues the key above it — a folded value, or a YAML list. The gate adjudicates the flat fields it names; a structured value is folded to one line and left to the reader.
parser.comments: a whole line beginning # is ignored, AND a trailing ' #' comment is stripped from a value — as YAML does. This is not a nicety: the taught examples carry their teaching in inline comments, so a parser that did NOT strip them made every faithfully-copied example unparseable. It did exactly that, silently, for as long as the examples have existed.
parser.unknown_fields: permitted and recorded. A gate that rejects an author for adding an honest extra field is a gate that punishes candour.
